The GEOTEC Journal Club is a **monthly, 60–70 minute session** where members discuss **one paper** to foster critical reading, debate and presentation: judging its methods, assumptions, results and contribution, as well as its academic writing style.

## Purpose

What it is
: A space to debate a paper's methods, assumptions, validity and writing, and to practise arguing about them.

What it is not
: A way to keep up to date with a specific field or subfield, although every paper has a clear link to GIScience. Members work on different topics, so selected papers will not always connect to each member's research.

Why it matters
: It develops transferable competences in the [ResearchComp](https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/jobs-research/researchcomp-european-competence-framework-researchers_en) framework, mainly *critical thinking*, *analytical thinking* and *evaluating research*.

## Who takes part

Open to all GEOTEC members: PhD students, faculty and other research profiles. Everyone takes a turn as facilitator.

## Format

| Item | Rule |
|:-----|:-----|
| Frequency | Monthly |
| Duration | 60–70 minutes |
| Papers per session | One |
| Paper length | Maximum 15 pages |
| Announcement | At least one week before the session |
| Facilitator | One person per session, on a rotation published at the start of each semester |

: Session format {#tbl-format}

Each session follows the same structure:

| Block | Led by | Time |
|:------|:-------|-----:|
| Context | Facilitator | 5 min |
| Summary | Facilitator | 10 min |
| Critical discussion | Everyone | 30–40 min |
| Takeaways | Everyone | 5–10 min |

: Session structure {#tbl-structure}

## Roles

Facilitator
: Selects the paper using the shared [selection criteria](paper-selection-criteria.qmd), announces it one week ahead, gives the context and summary, and guides the discussion.

Attendees
: Read the paper before the session and bring one question or critique.

## Ground rules

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
1. Everyone reads the paper, not only the facilitator.
2. Critique the paper, not the people.
3. "I didn't understand X" is a welcome contribution.
4. The shared guiding questions frame every discussion.
:::

## Record and review

- Each session is archived on the group's Quarto website: paper, facilitator, date, slides and key takeaways (see the [minutes template](minutes-template.qmd)).
- At the end of each semester (6 sessions), members hold a short retrospective and may propose changes to this charter.
